correctness.rationale: The claim holds for all real 1<p<infinity, sigma-finite infinite-dimensional Lp, all norm-one x and t>=0. For p<2, Hanner plus atomic coordinatewise Brézis--Lieb splitting and the proved derivative bound A_p(d,v)-A_p(d,u)<=v^p-u^p gives the universal lower bound. Balanced Rademacher signs on the finite weighted diffuse measure attain it, with weak-null rigor from L1 density and duality. For p>=2, scalar Clarkson supplies the lower bound and normalized disjoint indicators the weak-null equality sequence; t=0 and purely atomic x are covered. The companion numeric checker is nonexhaustive and is not substituted for any infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural sequential two-sided asymptotic norm profile is evaluated exactly across all mixed-measure sigma-finite real Lp spaces, not at a handpicked parameter. Its strict dependence only on nonatomic norm mass for 1<p<2, and complete loss of this dependence for p>=2, gives a sharp structural classification and exponent phase transition. The scalar mass-allocation lemma is essential rather than a mere substitution into a known global constant.
